findings.title: Caller can flush the terminal constraint trigger, then change the authoritative history before commit
findings.evidenceLevel: Concrete source/SQL-semantics counterexample; independent disposable PostgreSQL probe UNEXECUTED. Not a claimed failing root test.

paths.role: One-shot terminal receipt commit guard reads actual history here
Constraint event is receipt INSERT only and is caller-deferrable
History guard protects scope, not error_code/ended_at/snapshot_revision
Observed history guard protects binding/receipt; same binding with changed terminal history is allowed
REQUIRED deliberately joins external caller transaction

findings.canonicalRequirement: Current AC-14/design 4.1 and approved terminal-family Pax mapping require the exact actual winning terminal code/time/history snapshot at physical commit, independently of planned proposals and caller labels.
preconditions: Authentic publishedRetry fixture with remaining declared secret, QUEUED/PENDING accepted history and no admission
Outer caller transaction invokes the real public closeWithError; no savepoint, no trigger disable, no receipt rewrite or owner impersonation
reproduction: BEGIN outer transaction through fixture TransactionTemplate; call real closeWithError(id, DISPATCH_FAILED, now), require applied=1
SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE: existing deferred receipt event validates the consistent terminal ledger/history/summary and is consumed
UPDATE ui_test_executions SET error_code=DISPATCH_UNKNOWN, ended_at=ended_at + interval 1 second, snapshot_revision=snapshot_revision+1 WHERE id=<fixture id>
COMMIT; compare immutable receipt/ledger code and time and receipt.before_snapshot_revision+1 to history
findings.reason: The subsequent history UPDATE fires no terminal receipt INSERT event. Existing history triggers permit these three columns with unchanged binding/locator/scope. The DONE ledger code/time remains immutable, so the later history diverges from both ledger and receipt. PostgreSQL SET CONSTRAINTS explicitly forces pending constraint triggers early; their check is not automatically repeated at COMMIT without a new triggering event.
findings.expectedOracle: Reject the history mutation or roll back commit; require no committed receipt/audit/history/ledger inconsistency. Current source predicts a committed mismatch.
findings.rootTargetedProbe: Use the bounded standalone TerminalConstraintProbe source reproduced below with an own disposable publishedRetry fixture; no Gradle/shared results needed. Run only via root authorized database access. Record exact SQLSTATE/cause or committed mismatch count.
findings.recommendation: Make the authoritative invariant survive early constraint evaluation and all subsequent history mutations, or explicitly prohibit that caller path with database enforcement. Preserve exact terminal/top-XID/savepoint requirements; do not relax them.

findings.title: Future evidence partition is committed before its leaf constraint/TRUNCATE guards are installed
findings.evidenceLevel: Concrete two-statement visibility counterexample in current source; two-connection disposable PostgreSQL race UNEXECUTED. Existing green test inspects only completed installation.

paths.role: DO creation statement completes separately from guard installation
Second JdbcTemplate statement installs leaf-only guards
No surrounding transaction on production ensureAll
Daily creator invokes the same unwrapped path
No-send deferred guard is created only by installer
Terminal deferred guard is created only by installer

findings.canonicalRequirement: Current/future receipt leaves must enforce receipt+actual terminal winner+complete summaries, and direct-leaf append-only/TRUNCATE guarantees; parent-only checks or later completed setup are insufficient.
preconditions: Production bootstrap/scheduler uses JdbcTemplate autocommit with no surrounding transaction
Own new month outside initial current+2 leaves; actor has the ordinary SELECT/INSERT parent permissions, no DDL or trigger-disable authority
Authentic pre-transition owner/binding/declaration remains available; occurred_at is finite but no guard restricts it to wall-clock month
reproduction: Connection A executes exactly ensurePartition creation DO for a new terminal-receipt month and commits, then pauses before installSecretEvidenceGuards
Connection B observes the attached leaf and missing tr_observed_terminal_commit in pg_trigger

B inserts an otherwise authentic raw terminal settlement through the parent, with occurred_at in that month, captured before-image/full exact classification, then COMMIT without changing owner/history or appending summaries
A resumes installer; inspect the earlier committed receipt against still QUEUED/PENDING owner/history and absent summaries
findings.reason: Parent row INSERT guards are cloned, so they validate/capture pre-transition identity. The complete-winner constraint is a leaf trigger added only in the later statement; no event exists for B commit and a later CREATE TRIGGER does not validate prior rows. The advisory creation lock ends with the DO transaction and ordinary INSERT guards do not acquire that creation lock. A new receipt can therefore fence dispatch despite no terminal winner/usage settlement. A crash/failure between statements prolongs the same exposed state. Direct-leaf TRUNCATE guard is also absent until installation; ordinary append role still lacks TRUNCATE privilege.
findings.expectedOracle: At every visible attached-leaf state both constraint and direct-leaf guards exist; receipt-only commit must fail. Current source predicts visible unguarded interval and committed receipt-only cut.
findings.rootTargetedProbe: On an own disposable DB pause the production Java manager immediately after its first JDBC execute returns, without putting an outer test transaction around ensurePartition. Use second connection under actual least-writer role and an authentic receipt from the fixture. Capture pg_trigger before insertion and commit facts. This is not tested by checking after ensurePartition returns.
findings.recommendation: Publish attachment and all applicable leaf guards in one physical transaction, including already-existing leaf repair/failure semantics, while preserving no DEFAULT, append-only and prune behavior.

primarySources.title: PostgreSQL 15 SET CONSTRAINTS
primarySources.use: Caller switch to IMMEDIATE retroactively executes outstanding constraint triggers, which then obey statement-end timing.

primarySources.title: PostgreSQL 15 CREATE TRIGGER
primarySources.use: Constraint trigger event/time semantics; triggers act on their specified events and pending deferred firing can be forced by SET CONSTRAINTS.
